Tech-enablement theses by company

Each portfolio company gets a named operating system built on proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer. The aim is to make earnings look more recurring, predictable and scalable to the next buyer. The evidence supports up to ~3 turns of quality premium, with tech enablement able to claim about 0.5-2.5 turns depending on the company (ServiceOS evidence).

The six operating systems

Sources: ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan. The vendor-to-company mapping follows the order of the source list (est.).

Thesis by company

  • Punctual Pros (lead case): Lift booking rates from the 38% HVAC average toward the 59% seen at 25+ technician shops. Pricebook adopters grew tickets 14% vs 8%. The premium sits with membership-dense companies such as Champions (~18.5x, press estimate). Agents target missed calls, dispatch, options, memberships and permits (ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • CET: Turn project work into measured, recurring service lines, such as solar/SCADA O&M and NuWave and EV monitoring. Agents also improve bid selection and estimating speed. Buyers are more selective, with electrical M&A down to 99 deals in 2025.
  • Frontline: Build recurring security and e-billing revenue-cycle lines. The Aventis MSP curve runs from 5.2x to 11.2x. Entry was already ~12-15x (est.), which caps the upside.
  • Thomas Scientific: This is an EBITDA and cost-to-serve program, not a multiple story. Benchmarks are Avantor's ~80% digital transactions and Grainger's ~15.6% digital growth vs ~2% rep-led growth. The evidence is weak for a multiple premium, and capital structure dominates.
  • BPI: Productize monitoring into recurring revenue and protect client confidentiality while drafting faster. The PPHC ~8.4x floor compares with a 10-13x estimated sponsor exit.
  • Fair Harbor: Cut returns and excess inventory on a Shopify/Klaviyo stack. The premium range is truncated in the context. The full ServiceOS evidence file would answer it.

Caveats

  • Champions and Sila multiples are press estimates. Scaled roll-up prints mostly reflect scale and density, not technology.
  • All agent values are analyst assumptions and are not de-duplicated. The total is ~$12.7M (est.). Volumes must be replaced with system-of-record counts (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Next actions

  1. Pull call, ticket, invoice and member counts from each system of record to re-base the agent value estimates.
  2. Retrieve the Fair Harbor premium range and full HarborOS thesis from the complete ServiceOS evidence file.
  3. Set baselines for the wave 1 inbound-contact and document agents before launch, starting with the Punctual Pros missed-call booking rate.
  4. Stress-test the Frontline premium claim against its ~12-15x entry multiple (est.).
